answer: Running 199 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden honest participants do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the vault schedule in the orchard ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the thread checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 4 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. That is 32 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
